header.title: The token layer
header.description: Every visual decision in this system resolves to a token. Primitives hold the official brand values; semantic tokens describe intent. Components only ever consume the semantic layer, which is what makes a surface context switch — light, inverse, brand, corporate — work without a single component variant.

principles.title: Two layers, one direction of dependency
principles.description: Primitives are transcribed from the official RBI RGB palette and never referenced directly by a component. Semantic tokens alias them under intent-based names. The dependency only ever flows primitive → semantic → component.

yellow.title: Yellow is the signature
yellow.body: Primary yellow is reserved for the logo, the single primary action, and deliberate brand moments. It never becomes a body text colour and never fills a whole page behind dense content.

green.title: Green carries the corporate voice
green.body: The guidelines elevate corporate green for the international/corporate vertical. It is a secondary accent for ESG and sustainability content — never a substitute for yellow.

structure.title: Structure over decoration
structure.body: Borders, rules and generous space carry hierarchy. Shadows are reserved for genuinely floating surfaces, and radii stay small so the identity reads as precise rather than soft.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: Values are transcribed from Colour_Palette.zip (RBI - RGB - Full Palette.ase). Swatches below render from the live CSS custom property, so this page cannot drift from the implementation.

callout.title: Contrast is a property of the token pair, not the colour
callout.body: Primary yellow is a light colour: it takes off-black text, never white. Every text token documented here meets WCAG 2.2 AA against the surface it is paired with, and the accessible substitute for yellow text on white is --text-brand-accent (Yellow 700, 4.6:1).

paletteOverview.title: Palette overview
paletteOverview.description: The full primitive palette at a glance.

contrastChecker.title: Contrast checker
contrastChecker.description: Pick any two colours from the official palette and verify the pair against WCAG 2.2 before it reaches a component. Only palette colours are selectable, because a pair that passes with a colour we do not own is not a result.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Amalia is the RBI corporate typeface, self-hosted as WOFF2 in six weights plus italics. Weight does the work: Black for display statements, Bold for headings, Medium for UI labels, Regular for prose.

sizeScale.title: Size scale
sizeScale.description: A modular scale tuned for dense enterprise screens at the small end and editorial confidence at the large end. Body copy never drops below 16px.

letterSpacing.title: Letter spacing
letterSpacing.description: Display type is tightened; small all-caps labels are opened up so they stay legible.

spacing.title: Spacing and sizing
spacing.description: A 4px-based scale with deliberate jumps at the large end for section rhythm. Control heights are set so the default meets the WCAG 2.2 24px target-size minimum with room to spare.

shape.title: Shape and elevation
shape.description: Small radii keep the identity precise. Elevation is tinted with off-black rather than pure black so shadows stay warm and never look grey-blue.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: A 12-column grid with a 24px gutter, and four content widths so a form, a documentation page and a dense table each get an appropriate measure.

stackingOrder.title: Stacking order
stackingOrder.description: A fixed z-index ladder. Nothing in the system uses an arbitrary z-index value.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Motion is quick and purposeful: it confirms a state change rather than performing. Everything below is disabled outright under prefers-reduced-motion.

accessibility.title: Accessibility primitives
accessibility.description: The focus indicator is a system-level decision, not a per-component one. It is defined once in the base layer, never removed, and flips to yellow on inverse surfaces so it stays visible.

callout.title: What the tokens guarantee — and what they do not
callout.body: Tokens make correct contrast the default, but they cannot guarantee an accessible product. Semantics, focus order, names and roles still have to be right in each component — which is why every component on the Components page documents its keyboard and screen reader behaviour.

contrastChecker.sampleBody: Body copy at 14px on this pair, so the verdict below can be judged against something real.
contrastChecker.passSummary: This pair clears every AA threshold, including small body text.
contrastChecker.failSummary: This pair fails at least one AA threshold. Check the rows below for where it may still be used.
